subject: SunderTech inference fit & bench links — precision tradeoffs
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: SunderTech inference fit & bench links — precision tradeoffs

Hi Lina / SunderTech team,

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. This thread is a short post-call recap with concrete next steps so we can spin up a small evaluation that shows tradeoffs between throughput and quality across AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 approaches. Key takeaways from our discovery: 

- Workload: document-summarization + entity extraction for customer support tickets (~1.8k tokens average, 95% under 3k).
- Latency target: p50 <= 250ms for single-request path (interactive UI), p95 <= 700ms acceptable for batch workflows.
- Expected QPS for proof-of-concept: 40–60 reqs/sec sustained; peak bursts to 120.
- Primary quality metric: labeled-extractive F1 (entity extraction) + human-rated summary fidelity (1-5).

Recommended quick evaluation plan (48–72 hours to initial results):
1) Models to test (baseline -> compressed):
   - Redwood-Open-7B-v1 (FP16 baseline) — baseline for quality
   - Llama-2-13B (FP16) — comparison for increased capacity
   - Redwood-Open-7B-awq (AWQ 4-bit) — low-memory config
   - Llama-2-13B-gptq (GPTQ 4-bit) — throughput/quality comparison
   - Redwood-Open-7B-fp8 (experimental FP8 path) — if you want op-level FP8 trade point

2) Benchmarks we'll provide (attached + Drive link): token throughput, latency p50/p95, entity F1 on your sample label set, and a small human-blind A/B on summaries. Quick links: hubspot deal + drive folder included in metadata.

3) Prompt sets & evaluation harness: attached sundertech_promptset_v1.txt contains 120 representative prompts (mix of short/long tickets + edge cases). Please add any proprietary examples you want included and send back as a single CSV.

4) Decision criteria we suggest:
   - If AWQ 4-bit loses <2 F1 points vs FP16 and yields >2.5x token throughput improvement -> recommend AWQ for Dedicated pools.
   - If GPTQ 4-bit preserves >95% of baseline F1 with acceptable p95 latency, prefer GPTQ for low-latency interactive path.
   - Use FP8 only as an exploratory lane — quality sensitivity varies widely by headroom and kernel support; fallback path must be defined.

Immediate next steps I can own this week:
- Provision a 3-model small bench (Redwood-Open-7B FP16, Redwood-Open-7B AWQ, Llama-2-13B GPTQ) and run your prompt set.
- Deliver CSV summary + per-prompt diffs and a short deck with recommendation.

Can you confirm: 1) we have permission to run your attached prompt set on Redwood test environment? 2) do you want human A/B on a 30-sample subset (we can recruit an SME reviewer from your team)?

Attaching: sundertech_promptset_v1.txt, bench_results_summary.csv (example from internal pilot), redwood-quant-recs.pdf (brief).

Thanks — will schedule the bench once you confirm.

Best,
Priyom Das

- We can grant permission to run the attached prompt set in your Redwood test environment; confirming now.

Can you also add a quick row in the bench CSV that maps cost delta estimates (tokens/$) based on your throughput numbers? We need to show this to procurement.

Thanks — quick internal note and proposed acceptance criteria before we run: 

- Bench plan we will run (scripts automated):
  * Run baseline FP16 (Redwood-Open-7B) across 120 prompts, collect per-prompt latency, tokens, F1.
  * Run AWQ (4-bit) conversion on Redwood-Open-7B — measure throughput, p50/p95, entity F1 delta.
  * Run GPTQ (4-bit) on Llama-2-13B as alternate (note: different arch, will include cross-model normalization).
  * If time allows, run FP8 path on Redwood-Open-7B and include hallucination counts on the extraction set.

- Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
  * AWQ: entity F1 drop <= 2 points and p95 <= 700ms -> recommend for cost-first Dedicated lane.
  * GPTQ: entity F1 drop <= 1 point and p50 <= 300ms -> recommend for interactive lane.
  * FP8: exploratory only; must show no >3 point drop and hallucination delta < 1.5x baseline to consider.

- Cost delta row: we'll add an estimated tokens-per-dollar column based on your expected sustained QPS; include optional Dedicated pricing vs hosted comparison.

Action plan / schedule:
- Fri 21 Jul: provision bench and start runs (Priyom to approve infra).
- Mon 24 Jul: deliver preliminary CSV + short recommendation slide.

Lina — tagging you to confirm permission for us to run on the prompt set and to confirm SME for A/B. We'll include a shared Drive folder and a HubSpot update once runs start.
